meta.description: Assign cells to their sample of origin from cell or nucleus hashing and call cross-sample doublets using Seurat HTODemux/MULTIseqDemux, hashsolo, demuxEM, GMM-Demux, and demuxmix.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: All performance values in this report arise from explicitly seeded synthetic audit data and the retained logs; the skill makes no fabricated clinical or literature claims.

practice_boundaries.detail: The skill is limited to computational sample assignment and explicitly distinguishes it from genetic and expression-doublet methods; it makes no diagnosis or treatment recommendation.

methodological_ground.detail: Fresh runs support the stated method-selection logic: HTODemux/MULTIseq for clean tags, hashsolo for two tags with explicit noise barcodes, demuxmix with convergence review, and GMM-Demux for multiplet accounting.

code_usability.detail: The shipped Python and R examples parse, hashsolo executed with its documented parameter, and all five audit-owned dynamic code paths completed in the designated environment.

functional_suitability.note: The decision tables cover the promised HTO, MULTI-seq, CMO, ambient-background, and cross-sample-doublet cases; demuxEM is honestly bounded to Linux/Mac on this Windows audit host.

reliability.note: The skill identifies concrete failure modes and recovery actions, including hashsolo's two-tag degeneration, demuxmix underdispersion, and GMM output verification; it relies on the caller to inspect demuxmix convergence warnings.

performance_context.note: The 230-line skill is direct, sectional, and has only two focused examples without redundant workflow steps.

agent_usability.note: Clear method and parameter tables, explicit error symptoms, and grounded stop-and-diagnose thresholds make the workflow easy for an agent to apply; a concrete rare-tag validation snippet would remove the last inference burden.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language and the usage guide make the common assignment, doublet, weak-staining, and modality-choice requests discoverable.

security.note: No credentials, remote execution, or destructive operations are instructed. The examples assume locally trusted count-file paths and do not independently validate barcode alignment before assignment.

maintainability.note: Sections and examples are cleanly separated, but the skill ships no small HTO fixture or expected-output check for regression testing its documented edge cases.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision, composability with expression doublet detection, and explicit escape hatches are strong. Reruns were deterministic for hashsolo and GMM-Demux; only external caller state remains outside the skill.

inputs.label: Variable staining and underdispersed HTO background with demuxmix
inputs.note: A regular 540-cell three-tag run achieved 1.000 synthetic class agreement but surfaced demuxmix's documented non-convergence warning. A separate 600-cell near-constant background reproduced the glm.nb error and the skill's model='naive' fallback completed with 600 calls.
inputs.execution_note: Executed input3_demuxmix.R with the designated R 4.4.3 wrapper; evidence: run/phase2_20260923/input3.log.

assertions.note: It returned an HTO call table with 1.000 class agreement on this fixture.

assertions.text: The underdispersion failure mode is reproducible and explicit.

assertions.text: The documented naive-model fallback completes after that error.

inputs.label: Unequal four-CMO pool with a 5% minority tag
inputs.note: Fresh 900-cell stress run yielded 768 singlets, 66 doublets, and 66 negatives. After excluding unused factor levels, CMO-4 represented 0.047 of singlets, consistent with the planted 5% minority; the skill's 1/k=0.250 within-sample doublet reminder is correct for four pools.
inputs.execution_note: Executed input5_unequal_pooling.R with the designated R 4.4.3 wrapper; the initial factor-level observation and corrected agent-side inspection are both retained in input5_initial_factor_levels.log and input5.log.

assertions.text: The HTO workflow keeps a visibly rare but nonzero tag rather than declaring it absent.
assertions.note: CMO-4 accounted for 36 of 768 singlets, or 0.047.

assertions.text: The skill correctly describes the within-sample blind spot of hashing.
assertions.note: For k=4, the retained calculation reports the expected 1/k=0.250 fraction.

assertions.text: The stress response requires an orthogonal expression-doublet workflow rather than overclaiming HTO coverage.
assertions.note: The skill explicitly directs callers to expression doublet detection for same-sample doublets.

assertions.text: Rare-tag interpretation is robust to unused Seurat factor levels.
assertions.note: The audit response used droplevels before ranking actual singlet tags; the raw factor-level behavior is retained as a documentation improvement opportunity.

key_strengths: All core callable routes available on Windows in the designated environment executed fresh, including HTODemux, MULTIseqDemux, hashsolo, demuxmix, and GMM-Demux.
The two-tag hashsolo safeguard is both explicit in the source and effective in a fresh deterministic 700-cell run.
The demuxmix section accurately exposes a reproducible underdispersion failure and provides a successful model='naive' fallback while preserving the convergence warning.
The skill accurately keeps hashing, genetic demultiplexing, and expression-doublet detection as complementary rather than interchangeable methods.

recommendations.title: Add a rare-tag inspection snippet that drops unused levels
recommendations.problem: A direct table() over Seurat's factor-valued hash.ID can retain zero-count Doublet and Negative levels, so a naive minimum-tag calculation can falsely identify an unused level as the rarest tag.
recommendations.root_cause: The skill tells callers to inspect per-tag singlets but does not give a factor-safe code pattern for that stress check.
recommendations.fix: Add a short example such as table(droplevels(obj$hash.ID[obj$HTO_classification.global == 'Singlet'])) before applying a rare-tag threshold.

recommendations.title: Ship a small synthetic HTO regression fixture
recommendations.problem: The examples rely on caller-provided files, so agents cannot smoke-test the hashsolo, demuxmix, or GMM-Demux edge paths without first constructing data.
recommendations.root_cause: No deterministic example HTO matrix or expected call summary is bundled with the skill.
recommendations.fix: Add a tiny three- or four-tag CSV plus expected class counts and use it in the Python and CLI examples.
